ObjectName.value: Bird's eye view on two sailboats Beneteau Oceanis 411 from 15 m height (top of mast), photographer in a Bosun's chair doing repairs

Categories.value: Marinas in Andalusia|CC-Zero|Self-published work|Feet of the photographer|Sailboats in Spain|2004 photographs of Gibraltar|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Hiking sandals|Oceanis 411|People on bosun's chairs

ImageDescription.value: A bird's eye view on two nearly identical models of the sailboat Beneteau Oceanis 411 (12.50 m or 41 feet long) from 15 m height (top of mast), photographer in a Bosun's chair doing repairs. This was a training sailing trip for advanced yachtsmen/sailors starting in Tarifa, south of Spain, in 2004. When leaving the bay of Gibraltar in quite heavy, gusty winds but sun, a line needed for reducing the size of the main sail ripped, just when it was desperately needed due to the wind being too strong for the sailboat with the main sail at full size. Luckily, the situation was managed without any further damage. In the afternoon back in the marina (sport harbour) of Gibraltar, somebody had to go up (be pulled up in a textile chair called bosun's chair, more precise) to the mast top to replace the ripped line, which was the photographer and uploader doing this for the first time.

In the foreground is a Dehler 39 sailboat with a small inflatable dinghy in tow, and in the background is the Gäven lighthouse. The other boat is probably a Scampi. The islet closest to the camera is Skällholmen, next is Berggylteskär, followed by Gäven with the lighthouse, and last Trillingarna with only Skagerrak behind it.
